questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of London's sewer system and why it missed Soho
Florence Nightingale's nursing career and her work in London hospitals
How miasma theory was proven right by the 1854 Soho outbreak
John Snow's work linking the 1854 Soho cholera outbreak to a water pump
questions.explain: Snow's study traced the outbreak to the Broad Street pump, supporting the germ-in-water hypothesis.

questions.q: How many people died in the outbreak in total?
What did the authorities do to the Broad Street pump?
questions.explain: St James parish authorities disabled the pump by removing its handle.

questions.q: Why did workers at the nearby brewery avoid cholera?
options: They drank a daily beer allowance, made with boiled water
They were vaccinated by Snow before the outbreak began
They lived in housing outside Soho and rarely visited
They were quarantined inside the brewery for the outbreak's duration
questions.explain: They drank beer instead of pump water; brewing boils the wort and killed the bacteria.

questions.q: What does Snow's own comment imply about the pump handle removal?
options: It was ineffective because the water was in fact perfectly clean
Cases were already falling and residents had fled, so its effect is uncertain
It clearly ended the outbreak, as deaths fell immediately afterward
It caused deaths to rise as residents switched to other pumps
questions.explain: Snow said attacks had diminished before the water was stopped and it was impossible to decide.
